Profile Black and white mustard seeds have been used as emetics, in counter-irritant and rubefacient preparations, and as condiments. Volatile mustard oil, prepared from black mustard seeds, is large- ly composed of allyl isothiocyanate. It is an extremely powerful irritant that has been used as a counter-irritant and rubefacient. Expressed mustard oil contains a smaller proportion of volatile oil and has been used as a less powerful counter-irritant. Adverse effects. A report of 2 cases of IgE-mediated anaphy- laxis to mustard condiment.1 1. Vidal C, et al. Anaphylaxis to mustard. Postgrad Med J 1991; 67: 404. Handling. Allyl isothiocyanate is a potent lachrymator, with a pungent irritating odour. Care should be taken to protect the eyes, to prevent inhalation of fumes, and to avoid tasting.
